original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Speed up the complete pinned two-register D8 commutator replay through a packed two-column transition, retaining every original search, certificate and rejection control.
scope_change_reason: Refine the runtime card to one source-bound exact transition replacement. The predecessor mathematical theorem is cited, not an audit deliverable.
bottleneck_link: A small verifier-engineering result reduces repeated execution cost for this exact historical replay. It does not move the binding supplier or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop optimization at the first exact implementation with a reproducible complete-process speedup; retain follow-on ideas as questions.
evidence: README.md gives the transition-equivalence proof. verify.py checks 1,572,864 column cases, 67,800 reached-state transitions, complete ball witness maps, complete scientific results and eleven controls. BENCHMARK.json retains fifteen alternating fresh-process pairs with no failures.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can a direct table of complete column transitions repay its initialization and memory costs on a genuinely larger declared replay?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The current packed-byte method avoids a large table; a larger workload might amortize one.
open_questions.first_step: Choose and pin one larger complete replay, then count table initialization, storage and full-process time alongside exact conformance.
open_questions.blocked_by: No larger fixture or table implementation is supplied; the present result makes no such performance claim.
